narrative:
The 2022 Kansas City Royals were a team in transition, caught between the fading embers of their mid-decade dynasty and a youth movement that had not yet arrived in full force. They stumbled out of the gate in April, going 7-12, and May was even more brutal at 9-20 — a stretch defined by bullpen implosions, opponents' clutch hits, and a roster that simply lacked the firepower to compete night after night. The pitching staff bled runs at an alarming rate, and a 4.70 ERA season-wide told only part of the story of how many games slipped away in the late innings.

June and July offered a modest reprieve, with the Royals posting competitive records of 11-15 and 13-15 respectively. Bright spots emerged from unexpected places: young first baseman Vinnie Pasquantino debuted with immediate impact, slugging a go-ahead home run in July that gave a glimpse of the future. Salvador Perez, the heart of the franchise, continued to deliver in the clutch, including a stunning three-run blast against the Yankees on July 31st that stood as one of the season's most electric moments. Even as Aaron Judge and Shohei Ohtani took turns torching the Kansas City bullpen, the Royals fought with whatever pride they had left.

August and September brought a slow fade, the team going 13-16 and 10-16 as the losses mounted and the gaps in the roster became impossible to paper over. The bullpen, already overworked, continued to surrender critical leads. Carlos Hernández and Dylan Coleman were among those caught in damaging moments down the stretch, and a late-September series against Detroit piled on the indignities. The offense, ranked among the worst in baseball with a .686 OPS, simply could not manufacture enough runs to compensate for a pitching staff allowing 810 on the year.

The 2022 Royals finished 65-97, a sobering record that nonetheless contained seeds of hope. Pasquantino's debut, Melendez's emergence, and Perez's continued brilliance suggested the rebuild was not entirely stalled. But this was, at its core, a year of losing — of watching the bullpen surrender leads, of absorbing haymakers from the game's biggest stars, and of searching for an identity that had not yet fully taken shape. The future may belong to Kansas City, but 2022 was a year of paying dues.

chapters.title: A Rocky Start
chapters.description: The Royals stumble through April and into May, with the bullpen and rotation yielding costly hits to opponents in tight games.

chapters.title: May Mayhem
chapters.description: A brutal 9-20 May is punctuated by late-inning collapses, though Salvy Perez provides a rare clutch spark to keep hope alive.

chapters.title: Fighting Back in June and July
chapters.description: The Royals stabilize with back-to-back winning-adjacent months, fueled by Merrifield's leadership and Pasquantino's exciting debut.

chapters.title: Salvy's July Heroics
chapters.description: Salvador Perez delivers back-to-back clutch home runs against the mighty Yankees, giving Kansas City its most thrilling sequence of the season.

chapters.title: August Bright Spots
chapters.description: Nick Pratto and the young core flash their potential even as the team continues to tread water in the standings.

chapters.title: September Fade
chapters.description: The Royals collapse down the stretch, with the bullpen surrendering crucial leads and Detroit dealing final indignities in the season's closing weeks.
